dedupe_keys.name: geoportal de chile ide chile national catalogue of state geospatial layers including critical facilities public works and emergency layers

description: The Geoportal de Chile is the single access point to the geospatial data and services of the Chilean State, run by IDE Chile (the national spatial data infrastructure, formerly SNIT). On 28 September 2026 its catalogue listed 844 territorial data items from public bodies, with categories such as Instalaciones y edificaciones (facilities and buildings), Redes de energía y servicios básicos, Transporte, Aguas continentales and Planificación y catastro. Infrastructure-relevant layers found through its CSW include the national fire station register (Catastro Nacional de Cuarteles de Bomberos), police stations, health establishments 2026 (MINSAL), schools and nurseries (MINEDUC, JUNJI, Integra), the MOP public works, roads, hydraulic works and monitoring station layers, energy infrastructure, the SERNAGEOMIN tailings register, telecom antennas under the towers law, reservoirs, social housing and informal settlements (MINVU), and emergency layers from July 2026 such as water and power supply cut zones, shelters and the health network status. Coverage is national, with some regional layers; resolution is feature level. Format and access: OGC services (WMS and layers), shapefiles and PDF or XLS files, each with an ISO metadata record; the catalogue is harvestable through CSW (pycsw) at geoportal.cl/csw. Licence: not stated site-wide; users are asked to cite the providing institution named in each metadata record, and older mirrors on datos.gob.cl carry CC BY. Free. Caveats: download links mirrored on datos.gob.cl in 2024 now return 404, layer dates vary, and emergency layers are snapshots. Simulation uses: critical facility inventories for exposure and emergency response, network and asset layers for road and water systems, and event layers for validating outage and recovery models. Related records: Chile MOP GeoMOP, the INE Censo 2024 dwelling services table and the Chile public infrastructure project portfolio.
